disease.inheritance: X-linked recessive — DMD gene mutations (mostly out-of-frame deletions/duplications/nonsense)
disease.mechanism: Loss-of-function. Mutations in DMD abolish dystrophin, a large cytoskeletal protein that links the muscle fibre cytoskeleton to the extracellular matrix. Without dystrophin, muscle membranes are fragile and progressively degenerate, replaced by fibrosis and fat. This is a pure loss-of-function disease.
disease.autotac_rationale: NOT eligible. DMD is a loss-of-function disease — dystrophin is absent, not accumulated. Degrading any residual/truncated dystrophin would worsen the disease. Correct routes are dystrophin restoration: gene therapy (micro-dystrophin), exon skipping (to restore reading frame), and stop-codon readthrough.
disease.prevalence: ~1 in 3,500-5,000 live male births (commonly cited) — UNVERIFIED exact figure this session
disease.age_of_onset: Early childhood (2-5 years, motor delay and calf hypertrophy); wheelchair dependence ~age 12

approved_treatments.mechanism_correct: Corticosteroid that slows muscle degeneration by reducing inflammation; prolongs ambulation by several years. Does NOT restore dystrophin.
approved_treatments.note: Standard of care corticosteroid. Slows decline; does not correct the underlying dystrophin deficiency.

investigational: Gene therapy: delandistrogene moxeparvovec (Elevidys) — AAV micro-dystrophin (FDA accelerated approval 2023)
Exon-skipping ASOs: eteplirsen (exon 51), golodirsen (53), casimersen (45), viltolarsen (53)
Stop-codon readthrough: ataluren (translarna) — conditional approval in EU

disease.human_summary: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is the most common childhood muscular dystrophy, an X-linked disorder caused by dystrophin deficiency. Boys develop progressive muscle weakness from early childhood, losing ambulation in their teens and dying from respiratory or cardiac failure in young adulthood. Gene therapy and exon-skipping are the leading disease-modifying approaches.
